blocks.text: The herd is the unit, not the chat.

content.value: herdr (github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr, 17.7k stars) proves a market thesis: what users of agent fleets want most is glanceability — every agent classified working/blocked/idle at a glance, that state rolled up pane→tab→workspace, one event subscription for the whole fleet, and attach/detach that never kills the agent. Our tuning of that thesis: the herd is built for extended autopilot — long unattended runs where the only question is 'is anything asking for me, and is everything else actually still moving?' Barkpark Chat already owns the harder half: durable Postgres transcripts with SSE Last-Event-ID resume, structured stream-json frames instead of PTY scraping, multi-tenancy, cost accounting, and cloud/remote execution targets. The herd layer is mostly derivation and UX over frames the Recorder already persists.

blocks.text: What we deliberately do NOT copy

content.value: PTY-faithful terminal rendering (herdr scrapes screens because it is blind; we own the wire — pdrender block rendering is what makes two-surface parity and persistence possible). The tmux prefix-key model (Bubble Tea + existing mouse work covers interaction). A chat-pane plugin marketplace (Barkpark.Plugin is already the extension seam; speculative here). herdr's TOML screen-manifest fallback (we have no screen to scrape — but we keep its discipline: authoritative reporters are the ONLY truth source when present, and any heuristic is strict about 'blocked', because a false blocked trains users to ignore the signal).

blocks.value:
permission/ask frame pending ............ blocked   (needs you)
deltas flowing (turn active) ............ working   (autopilot)
result frame landed, nothing pending .... idle
runner process gone / host lease lost ... unknown   (possibly wedged)

no read/unread tracking anywhere — "seen" never matters.
the one axis: autopilot vs needs-attention.

stall = working AND no frame for longer than a threshold
        (a view-side badge from agent_state_at + last-frame age,
         not a fifth state — the column stays honest)

session.agent_state --rollup--> workspace state --> "anything blocked anywhere?"
precedence for rollup: blocked > working > unknown > idle

content.value: agent_state is a column on chat_sessions, written by the Recorder in the same transaction as the sidebar denormalizations (append_message already does this for counts/costs — same seam, same change-only discipline as the wave-5 activity overlay). The derivation is authoritative because we speak stream-json: a pending approval IS blocked, a result frame with nothing pending IS idle. No polling, no inference, and deliberately no read receipts — a session that finished a turn is simply idle; the herd exists so you can leave sessions on autopilot for hours and trust two signals: blocked floats to you, and working proves its own liveness (fresh agent_state_at / now-line) or earns a stall badge.

The substrate. Recorder derives the four-state enum (working/blocked/idle/unknown) from frames it already handles; chat_sessions grows agent_state + agent_state_at; StudioChat exposes a per-workspace rollup (counts by state + highest-precedence state). agent_state_at doubles as the liveness clock: working with a stale timestamp is what the herd view renders as stalled. Sidebar pill and needs-you strip re-base onto it — the wsc session-card pill becomes a reader of this column instead of a parallel derivation. Explicitly NOT here: read receipts or any seen/unseen bookkeeping.

herdr clients hold ONE socket subscription and receive agent_status_changed for everything; our SSE is per-session, so N sessions cost N streams today. One scope-gated SSE endpoint emitting state-change frames only (session id, state, ts, title — never content), with Last-Event-ID replay like the session stream. apiclient grows the binding. This powers the live sidebar without polling, bp chat ls --watch, the herd view, and notifications — all from one connection.

blocks.text: s3 — the herd view in bp chat

content.value: The multiplexer home screen, sorted by attention: blocked floats to the top, then stalled (working but frame-quiet past the threshold, badged from agent_state_at), then working with its live now-line proving liveness, then idle. Enter attaches, esc detaches back to the herd (the engine already guarantees the agent keeps running — we only expose the UX). Driven by the fleet stream, cold-mounted from the sessions list. This is the feature users would call 'next level'; s1+s2 are its substrate. Builds on the wsc session-list lines rather than replacing them.

blocks.text: s4 — MCP session tools: agents herd agents

content.value: herdr's socket API lets agents spawn panes, read siblings, and coordinate — 'agents can use herdr themselves.' Our analog: session primitives on the loopback MCP server and bp mcp serve — chat_spawn_session, chat_send, chat_read_tail, chat_wait_for_state. An agent in one session herds sub-sessions on autopilot, each with its own transcript, cost line, permission gate, and tenancy — which herdr cannot offer. chat_wait_for_state waits on working→idle or →blocked, so the herder sleeps between turns instead of polling. Discipline kept: the CLI/MCP stay thin wrappers over /v1/chat, never a second path.

Session blocked longer than a threshold → push through the existing notification seams (webhook first; openclaw/Discord adapters ride it). Trivial once s1 exists; it is what makes walking away from a running herd safe. Debounced, per-session, cleared on unblock.

Registered remote hosts (chat_hosts) will eventually run agents we do not speak stream-json with. herdr's answer is the right shape: an explicit authoritative report call (their pane.report_agent) installed as a lifecycle hook. Ours: POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/state, epoch-fenced like host leases, accepting the same four-state vocabulary; when a reporter is active it is the only truth source for that session. The Codex runtime maps its native states onto the same enum.

blocks.value:
s1 agent_state column ──▶ s2 fleet SSE ──▶ s3 herd view (bp chat)
        │                      └──────────▶ s5 blocked notifications
        ├──────────────────────────────────▶ s4 MCP session tools (reads state via s1; stream optional)
        └──────────────────────────────────▶ s6 report_state (writes into s1's column)

content.value: No overlap in deliverables: wsc is per-session presentation (workflow lines on the card, drill-down, steer); the herd layer is the semantic substrate (state column), fleet transport (one stream), the multiplexer home, and agent-facing orchestration. The wsc pill and needs-you strip become readers of agent_state (s1), and the herd view (s3) reuses the wsc session-list lines. Where wsc-bl-workflow-sse widened the single-session wire, s2 adds the cross-session wire.

Load-bearing discovery: the state machine already exists. Recorder.activity_topic() (recorder.ex:91-98, wave 5) already broadcasts {:chat_activity, session_id, %{state: :working | :needs_you | :idle | :offline, line}} change-only. s1 is therefore: persist that existing derivation (mapping needs_you→blocked, offline→unknown) instead of inventing a new one. Also verified: chat_controller.ex has full seq/Last-Event-ID replay machinery with public seams (replay_events/2:460, sse_chat_frame/1:476); chat_hosts/protocol.ex has the epoch fence returning :stale_fence; internal/chat/reduce.go is a pure typed-event reducer (FrameEvent/TickEvent/... — a herd screen is new events + state, no architecture change); claude_chat.ex owns the loopback MCP config builder.

blocks.value:
wave 1 — engine (Elixir)
  PR-1 s1: migration (agent_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'idle' + agent_state_at,
           index on (owner_workspace_id, agent_state)); persist AT the wave-5
           derivation seam, FLIPS ONLY + coarse heartbeat (60s while working) —
           never per-delta; boot sweep marks orphaned working/blocked → unknown;
           workspace rollup query; pill + needs-you strip become readers.
  PR-2 s2: FleetHub GenServer (subscribes activity_topic, monotonic seq,
           ring of last 256 flips); GET /v1/chat/events = snapshot frame on
           connect, then live flips; Last-Event-ID in-ring → replay, older →
           fresh snapshot (gap-free by convergence); apiclient binding.

wave 2 — surfaces (parallel, zero shared files)
  PR-3 s3 (Go): herd home screen in reduce.go events; attach/detach;
           stall badge from TickEvent vs last-frame age; ls --watch.
  PR-4 s5 (Elixir): blocked flip → send_after(+threshold) → still same ask?
           → webhook chat.session.blocked; unblock cancels; keyed dedupe.

wave 3 — orchestration
  PR-5 s4: four MCP tools on loopback server + bp mcp serve; wait_for_state
           subscribes PubSub w/ bounded timeout (sleep, not poll).
  PR-6 s6: POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/state through Protocol.accept epoch
           fence; reporter-active suspends Recorder-derived writes.

content.value: Risks + mitigations. (1) Per-delta DB writes would melt the store — policy is flips-only + 60s heartbeat; live stall ticks ride PubSub, the column is for cold truth. (2) recorder.ex/chat_live.ex are hot wsc files — s1 builds solo in its worktree before anything else touches them; open wsc backlog tasks don't collide with the flip-persist seam. (3) False blocked destroys trust — only explicit ask frames or reporter calls may set it (guarded + tested, s6). (4) BEAM restart honesty — boot sweep + :offline mapping means a dead runner can never show working. (5) Gates: every Elixir PR waits for the blocking Elixir Test gate; merged = live on guerrilla, so each wave ends with a real smoke: curl -N /v1/chat/events while driving a session from bp chat and watching working→idle flip on the wire.

(1) Stall threshold: fixed default (e.g. 3–5 min without a frame while working) or per-workspace setting — and should long tool calls (Bash builds) get a softer badge? (2) Does the fleet stream carry the wsc workflow summary lines or state-only frames? Lean state-only; the herd view fetches lines on mount. (3) chat_wait_for_state long-poll timeout vs MCP tool-call timeout budget. (4) Should workspace rollup surface in /v1/capabilities for the Studio shell badge, or stay a chat-scope endpoint?

(2) Does the fleet stream carry the wsc workflow summary lines or state-only frames? Lean state-only; the herd view fetches lines on mount. body_html:
Design · Barkpark Chat · 2026-07-18 · herd-layer epic

The herd is the unit, not the chat.

herdr (github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr, 17.7k stars) proves a market thesis: what users of agent fleets want most is glanceability — every agent classified working/blocked/idle at a glance, that state rolled up pane→tab→workspace, one event subscription for the whole fleet, and attach/detach that never kills the agent. Our tuning of that thesis: the herd is built for extended autopilot — long unattended runs where the only question is 'is anything asking for me, and is everything else actually still moving?' Barkpark Chat already owns the harder half: durable Postgres transcripts with SSE Last-Event-ID resume, structured stream-json frames instead of PTY scraping, multi-tenancy, cost accounting, and cloud/remote execution targets. The herd layer is mostly derivation and UX over frames the Recorder already persists.

What we deliberately do NOT copy

PTY-faithful terminal rendering (herdr scrapes screens because it is blind; we own the wire — pdrender block rendering is what makes two-surface parity and persistence possible). The tmux prefix-key model (Bubble Tea + existing mouse work covers interaction). A chat-pane plugin marketplace (Barkpark.Plugin is already the extension seam; speculative here). herdr's TOML screen-manifest fallback (we have no screen to scrape — but we keep its discipline: authoritative reporters are the ONLY truth source when present, and any heuristic is strict about 'blocked', because a false blocked trains users to ignore the signal).

The state machine

permission/ask frame pending ............ blocked   (needs you)
deltas flowing (turn active) ............ working   (autopilot)
result frame landed, nothing pending .... idle
runner process gone / host lease lost ... unknown   (possibly wedged)

no read/unread tracking anywhere — "seen" never matters.
the one axis: autopilot vs needs-attention.

stall = working AND no frame for longer than a threshold
        (a view-side badge from agent_state_at + last-frame age,
         not a fifth state — the column stays honest)

session.agent_state --rollup--> workspace state --> "anything blocked anywhere?"
precedence for rollup: blocked > working > unknown > idle

agent_state is a column on chat_sessions, written by the Recorder in the same transaction as the sidebar denormalizations (append_message already does this for counts/costs — same seam, same change-only discipline as the wave-5 activity overlay). The derivation is authoritative because we speak stream-json: a pending approval IS blocked, a result frame with nothing pending IS idle. No polling, no inference, and deliberately no read receipts — a session that finished a turn is simply idle; the herd exists so you can leave sessions on autopilot for hours and trust two signals: blocked floats to you, and working proves its own liveness (fresh agent_state_at / now-line) or earns a stall badge.

Six moves

s1 — agent_state column + workspace rollup

The substrate. Recorder derives the four-state enum (working/blocked/idle/unknown) from frames it already handles; chat_sessions grows agent_state + agent_state_at; StudioChat exposes a per-workspace rollup (counts by state + highest-precedence state). agent_state_at doubles as the liveness clock: working with a stale timestamp is what the herd view renders as stalled. Sidebar pill and needs-you strip re-base onto it — the wsc session-card pill becomes a reader of this column instead of a parallel derivation. Explicitly NOT here: read receipts or any seen/unseen bookkeeping.

s2 — fleet event stream: GET /v1/chat/events

herdr clients hold ONE socket subscription and receive agent_status_changed for everything; our SSE is per-session, so N sessions cost N streams today. One scope-gated SSE endpoint emitting state-change frames only (session id, state, ts, title — never content), with Last-Event-ID replay like the session stream. apiclient grows the binding. This powers the live sidebar without polling, bp chat ls --watch, the herd view, and notifications — all from one connection.

s3 — the herd view in bp chat

The multiplexer home screen, sorted by attention: blocked floats to the top, then stalled (working but frame-quiet past the threshold, badged from agent_state_at), then working with its live now-line proving liveness, then idle. Enter attaches, esc detaches back to the herd (the engine already guarantees the agent keeps running — we only expose the UX). Driven by the fleet stream, cold-mounted from the sessions list. This is the feature users would call 'next level'; s1+s2 are its substrate. Builds on the wsc session-list lines rather than replacing them.

s4 — MCP session tools: agents herd agents

herdr's socket API lets agents spawn panes, read siblings, and coordinate — 'agents can use herdr themselves.' Our analog: session primitives on the loopback MCP server and bp mcp serve — chat_spawn_session, chat_send, chat_read_tail, chat_wait_for_state. An agent in one session herds sub-sessions on autopilot, each with its own transcript, cost line, permission gate, and tenancy — which herdr cannot offer. chat_wait_for_state waits on working→idle or →blocked, so the herder sleeps between turns instead of polling. Discipline kept: the CLI/MCP stay thin wrappers over /v1/chat, never a second path.

s5 — blocked-state notifications

Session blocked longer than a threshold → push through the existing notification seams (webhook first; openclaw/Discord adapters ride it). Trivial once s1 exists; it is what makes walking away from a running herd safe. Debounced, per-session, cleared on unblock.

s6 — report_state for foreign agents

Registered remote hosts (chat_hosts) will eventually run agents we do not speak stream-json with. herdr's answer is the right shape: an explicit authoritative report call (their pane.report_agent) installed as a lifecycle hook. Ours: POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/state, epoch-fenced like host leases, accepting the same four-state vocabulary; when a reporter is active it is the only truth source for that session. The Codex runtime maps its native states onto the same enum.

Dependency spine

s1 agent_state column ──▶ s2 fleet SSE ──▶ s3 herd view (bp chat)
        │                      └──────────▶ s5 blocked notifications
        ├──────────────────────────────────▶ s4 MCP session tools (reads state via s1; stream optional)
        └──────────────────────────────────▶ s6 report_state (writes into s1's column)

Relationship to the session-card (wsc) epic

No overlap in deliverables: wsc is per-session presentation (workflow lines on the card, drill-down, steer); the herd layer is the semantic substrate (state column), fleet transport (one stream), the multiplexer home, and agent-facing orchestration. The wsc pill and needs-you strip become readers of agent_state (s1), and the herd view (s3) reuses the wsc session-list lines. Where wsc-bl-workflow-sse widened the single-session wire, s2 adds the cross-session wire.

Build plan (verified against the code 2026-07-18)

Load-bearing discovery: the state machine already exists. Recorder.activity_topic() (recorder.ex:91-98, wave 5) already broadcasts {:chat_activity, session_id, %{state: :working | :needs_you | :idle | :offline, line}} change-only. s1 is therefore: persist that existing derivation (mapping needs_you→blocked, offline→unknown) instead of inventing a new one. Also verified: chat_controller.ex has full seq/Last-Event-ID replay machinery with public seams (replay_events/2:460, sse_chat_frame/1:476); chat_hosts/protocol.ex has the epoch fence returning :stale_fence; internal/chat/reduce.go is a pure typed-event reducer (FrameEvent/TickEvent/... — a herd screen is new events + state, no architecture change); claude_chat.ex owns the loopback MCP config builder.

wave 1 — engine (Elixir)
  PR-1 s1: migration (agent_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'idle' + agent_state_at,
           index on (owner_workspace_id, agent_state)); persist AT the wave-5
           derivation seam, FLIPS ONLY + coarse heartbeat (60s while working) —
           never per-delta; boot sweep marks orphaned working/blocked → unknown;
           workspace rollup query; pill + needs-you strip become readers.
  PR-2 s2: FleetHub GenServer (subscribes activity_topic, monotonic seq,
           ring of last 256 flips); GET /v1/chat/events = snapshot frame on
           connect, then live flips; Last-Event-ID in-ring → replay, older →
           fresh snapshot (gap-free by convergence); apiclient binding.

wave 2 — surfaces (parallel, zero shared files)
  PR-3 s3 (Go): herd home screen in reduce.go events; attach/detach;
           stall badge from TickEvent vs last-frame age; ls --watch.
  PR-4 s5 (Elixir): blocked flip → send_after(+threshold) → still same ask?
           → webhook chat.session.blocked; unblock cancels; keyed dedupe.

wave 3 — orchestration
  PR-5 s4: four MCP tools on loopback server + bp mcp serve; wait_for_state
           subscribes PubSub w/ bounded timeout (sleep, not poll).
  PR-6 s6: POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/state through Protocol.accept epoch
           fence; reporter-active suspends Recorder-derived writes.

Risks + mitigations. (1) Per-delta DB writes would melt the store — policy is flips-only + 60s heartbeat; live stall ticks ride PubSub, the column is for cold truth. (2) recorder.ex/chat_live.ex are hot wsc files — s1 builds solo in its worktree before anything else touches them; open wsc backlog tasks don't collide with the flip-persist seam. (3) False blocked destroys trust — only explicit ask frames or reporter calls may set it (guarded + tested, s6). (4) BEAM restart honesty — boot sweep + :offline mapping means a dead runner can never show working. (5) Gates: every Elixir PR waits for the blocking Elixir Test gate; merged = live on guerrilla, so each wave ends with a real smoke: curl -N /v1/chat/events while driving a session from bp chat and watching working→idle flip on the wire.

Open questions

(1) Stall threshold: fixed default (e.g. 3–5 min without a frame while working) or per-workspace setting — and should long tool calls (Bash builds) get a softer badge? (2) Does the fleet stream carry the wsc workflow summary lines or state-only frames? Lean state-only; the herd view fetches lines on mount. (3) chat_wait_for_state long-poll timeout vs MCP tool-call timeout budget. (4) Should workspace rollup surface in /v1/capabilities for the Studio shell badge, or stay a chat-scope endpoint?
description: Design: the herd layer for Barkpark Chat, distilled from herdr (the 17.7k-star Rust agent multiplexer), tuned for extended autopilot runs. The one axis that matters: autopilot vs needs-attention — no read/unread tracking anywhere. Six moves: a first-class semantic agent_state on every chat session (working/blocked/idle/unknown) derived from frames the Recorder already owns, plus stall detection for working-but-quiet sessions; workspace rollup; one fleet SSE event stream (/v1/chat/events); a multiplexer herd home view in bp chat with attach/detach; MCP session tools so agents can herd sub-sessions; blocked-state notifications; and an authoritative report_state channel for foreign agents on registered remote hosts. Explicit non-goals: PTY-faithful rendering, tmux prefix keys, a chat-pane plugin marketplace, read receipts. Drives the herd-layer epic and its six slices.
